title: Thoughts on using Suno AI for music?
author: Individual-Loquat542
selftext: Hi, I'm a solo indie gamedev who has zero musical talent whatsoever. I was considering using Suno for my game's music, but apparently you need a license and the more I looked into it, the more I was unsure. What are the running opinions on using Suno for gamedev? Is it good enough, does it sound good? What are your thoughts?

comments.author: MusicalMadnes
comments.body: always read the contracts on ai music platforms, personally i use udio but not for game development at this current point in time. Most people probably prefer suno but udio is more controllable imo

replies.author: Agile-Music-2295
replies.body: Udio sounds considerably better. Especially vocals.

comments.body: You got a have the subscription for the rights to use it. Not a big deal, it's like $10 a month or so. There is also free and open source alternatives you can try out on your own machine like Yue, Ace Step, Stable Audio, etc.

comments.body: From what I've seen and heard, it's ok, but the result is more important than the tool.

comments.author: Galactic_Neighbour
comments.body: There is ACE-Step, which is a model you can run on your computer. It's not great, but maybe it's something to watch out for in the future. Perhaps you could make some placeholders with it, though.

comments.author: PyjamaKooka
comments.body:
I've been experimenting with AI music for over a year. Pretty dedicated to Suno at this point, but mostly just preference and idiosyncracies (Suno makes weird stuff I like). 

With each big version leap (3, 3.5, 4, and now 4.5) there's quite a leap and the latest one is getting really damn good. I've been using it for all kinds of projects from music videos to more recently, scoring my game. I reckon everyone has musical talent, the trick is to play around with it and explore. It's all about tweaking inputs, thinking about prompts etc. 

I'm experienced with music making/production and a bit of software around all that, but even with all that I think Suno makes great stuff a lot of the time and unless I'm going all out on a track I don't often feel the need to add anything except some basic mastering, which you can also do yourself free online various places (Bandlab has a good unlimted free service for example). 

If you want some varied samples of Suno stuff, made with 4.5 just go browse it there's obviously countless tracks piling out, but if you wanna see some with love and care put into 'em plz do check some of mine out if you wanna: here's some [horror techno ambience](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x9vaPk2T8dA), [a sombre minimalist violin score for a scene opening](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OWVNT5KFp6Y), or [another orchestral score with pizzicato and some lyrics](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A2SZtey8biE) for example. :)

comments.author: interestingsystems
comments.body: What is the latest on an API for either Suno or Udio?

comments.author: IfnotFr
comments.body: Suno can produce surprisingly decent music for indie games, but licensing is a real issue. For commercial projects, double-check the terms - or look into royalty-free AI options instead.
